high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Ajrakh block-printed illustration: a Khatri printer compares two identical eight-petal impressions with a separate nine-petal proof, all figures, blocks and cloths assembled from flat indigo, madder, black and cream repeats on cotton; no gradients, modeled depth, writing or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: One continuous cream cotton field fills the frame, structured by an indigo outer border, a madder-red inner lattice, black stepped diamonds, and small cream reserve dots. A single central working register interrupts the repeats without creating a room or window. No horizon, realistic floor, receding perspective, shop sign, script, numeral, caption, arrow, diagram, religious image, national emblem, certification seal, computer, fashion display, ranking device, or museum vitrine appears.

elements.desc: Experienced Khatri Ajrakh printer standing behind the worktable, medium-brown skin, short black hair graying at the temples, trimmed beard, cream cotton kurta, indigo apron, loose brown trousers, and dark sandals. He compares the old and new proof edges with a focused practical expression, keeping both designs present and carrying no judge’s badge, medal, signature tool, or ceremonial object.

Long padded Ajrakh printing table angled across the central register, reduced to one cream rectangle with indigo legs and surrounded only by two madder dye trays, a folded wiping cloth, and four registration pins. It supports the old block, new block, and three proofs as production materials rather than a symmetrical exhibition or quality-ranking display.

First old-design proof lying flat at the lower-left table edge, printed in indigo, madder red, black, and cream. Its repeat unit contains an eight-petal central rosette inside two interlocking star frames, bordered by paired dots and small stepped diamonds; the fabric carries no writing, maker mark, label, number, figurative scene, or separate emblem.

Second old-design proof folded once beneath the first, made from the same cotton and displaying the exact same eight-petal rosette, interlocking star frames, paired dots, stepped diamonds, colors, scale, and registration. Its visible repeat is unchanged and remains physically present beside the new proof, without correction mark, deletion, overprint, label, or ranking sign.

New-design proof resting separately at the lower-right end of the table, using the same indigo, madder red, black, cream, scale, border, dots, and star frames as the old proofs. Its central rosette alone has nine petals instead of eight, making the changed design visibly distinct without claiming superiority, replacing the earlier cloths, or adding text.

Worn square teak printing block resting face-up above the two old proofs, its carved surface showing one eight-petal rosette, two star frames, paired dots, and stepped diamonds in reverse relief. Indigo and madder traces remain in the grooves; the block has a rounded handgrip but no inscription, numeral, religious motif, maker seal, certification mark, or damage.

New square teak printing block resting face-up directly above the separate new proof, matching the old block in dimensions, handgrip, star frames, dots, and diamonds. Only its central reverse-relief rosette carries nine clean petals. Fresh pale wood distinguishes the recarved design without crown, label, date, badge, signature, decorative animal, or authority symbol.
